sanskrit: yasyedam ā rajo yujas tuje janaṃ vanaṃ svaḥ | indrasya nādhṛṣe śavaḥ ||
english: Whose might encompasses dust, comrades, struggle, people, forest, and heaven — the power of Indra is not to be withstood.

sanskrit: dhṛṣāṇaṃ dhṛṣataḥ śavaḥ purā yathāyatiṣṭhan | indrasya rantyaṃ mahat ||
english: The bold strength of the bold one — as of old it stood firm — great is the exhilarating power of Indra.

sanskrit: sa no dadhātu taṃ rayiṃ puruṃ piśaṅgapeśasam | indraḥ patis tuviṣṭamo janeṣv ā ||
english: May he bestow upon us that wealth, abundant, tawny-hued — Indra, the most mighty lord among the peoples.

sanskrit: āyur agna ihā vaha jātavedas tanūvaśin | yathāhaṃ jyog ihāsāni prajānām adhipā vaśī ||
english: Bring life-span hither, O Agni, O Jātavedas, master of bodies, so that I may dwell here long as sovereign ruler over my progeny.

sanskrit: āyur indro dadhātu ma āyur devo bṛhaspatiḥ | āyur me viśve devā ahorātre ca cakratuḥ ||
english: May Indra bestow life-span upon me; may the god Bṛhaspati bestow life-span; may all the gods and Day-and-Night create life-span for me.

sanskrit: āyur āyuṣyā pavatāṃ prāṇaṃ prāṇo dadhātu me | devā yac cakrur devebhyaḥ svar yanto yathāyatham ||
english: May the life-giving one purify life-span; may breath bestow breath upon me — that which the gods have fashioned for the gods, going to the heavenly light in due order.

sanskrit: utpatantu nabhasvatīḥ samudrād adhi ghoṣiṇīḥ | utsyāḥ samudriyā apas tābhiṣ ṭvā tarpayāmasi ||
english: Let the cloud-bearing, roaring waters rise up from the ocean; let the spring waters, the sea-born waters — with those we gratify you.

sanskrit: yā āpo divyā yā vātāt parijajñire | indro marutvāṃs tṛptātmā tābhiṣ ṭvā tarpayāmasi ||
english: The waters that are celestial, those that were born around the wind — Indra with the Maruts, of satisfied spirit: with those we gratify you.

sanskrit: yāḥ śuṣkā yā hariṇīr yā bhūmim anuvāvṛdhuḥ | sarvāḥ samagrā oṣadhīs tābhiṣ ṭvā tarpayāmasi ||
english: The herbs that are dry, those that are green, those that have grown along the earth — all the herbs together: with those we gratify you.

sanskrit: ā no medhā sumatir viśvarūpā giro bṛhatīr āveśayantī | ṛco me bahvīr ny anaktu gā iva yathāsāma bhuvaneṣu karṇinaḥ ||
english: May insight and good-thought of all forms enter into us, bringing mighty hymns; may the many Ṛk verses anoint me like cows, so that we may be listeners in the worlds.

sanskrit: dīkṣā tapo manaso mātariśvā bṛhaspatir vāco asyāḥ sa yoniḥ | vedāṃsi vidyā mayi santu bahvīr agnīṣomā yaśo asmāsu dhattam ||
english: Consecration, ardor, the breath of the mind — Bṛhaspati is the source of this speech; may the Vedas, may knowledge in abundance abide in me. O Agni and Soma, bestow glory upon us.

sanskrit: yad agne tapasā tapa upaprekṣāmahe vayam | priyāḥ śrutasya bhūyāsma- -āyuṣmantaḥ sumedhasaḥ ||
english: O Agni, when we gaze upon the heat with ardor — may we be dear to sacred learning, long-lived and of good intelligence.

sanskrit: yas tvā mātur uta vā pituḥ parijāyamānam abhisaṃbabhūva | taṃ tvad yakṣmam adhi nāśayāmaḥ so 'nyasmiṃ chrayātai praviṣṭaḥ ||
english: The disease that overcame you as you were born from your mother or from your father — that wasting illness we drive away from you; let it enter and take refuge in another.

sanskrit: yas te yakṣmo hṛdayeṣṭho nābhiṣṭhā udaraṃgamaḥ | atho yaḥ śiśriye parau taṃ tvad yakṣmam adhi nāśayāmaḥ so 'nyasmiṃ chrayātai praviṣṭaḥ ||
english: The wasting disease that lodges in your heart, that stands in the navel, that penetrates the belly, and that which clings in the extremities — that wasting illness we drive away from you; let it enter and take refuge in another.

sanskrit: śīrṣarogam aṅgarogaṃ snāvabṛham abhiśāciṃ visalpakam | yas te yakṣmo majjasu paruḥsu yo gudāsu taṃ tvad yakṣmam adhi nāśayāmaḥ so 'nyasmiṃ chrayātai praviṣṭaḥ ||
english: Head-disease, limb-disease, the swelling of the sinews, the evil curse, the spreading eruption — the wasting disease in your marrow, in your joints, in your bowels — that wasting illness we drive away from you; let it enter and take refuge in another.

sanskrit: agnī rakṣohā tigmas tigmaśṛṅgo hantu rakṣo nudatām arātim | apāghaśaṃsam asyatu ||
english: Agni the demon-slayer, sharp, sharp-horned — let him smite the demon, thrust away the enemy, and shoot away the ill-proclaimer.

sanskrit: ā ta etu parāvato balam ojo divas pari | ā giribhyaḥ parvatebhya āyuṣ ṭe viśvato dadhat ||
english: Let strength and vigor come to you from the distant realm, from all around heaven; from the hills and mountains, bestowing life-span upon you from all sides.

sanskrit: punas te 'suṃ pṛthivī dadātu punar dyaur devo punar antarikṣam | punas te somas tanvaṃ dadhātu punaḥ pūṣā pathyāṃ yā svastiḥ ||
english: May the earth give your breath back to you again; may divine heaven, may the atmosphere give it back again; may Soma restore your body again; may Pūṣan restore the path that leads to well-being.

sanskrit: kaṣkiṣā kaṣpiṣā yevāṣā eṣā | iṣṭargava iṣayantaḥ saikatāḥ pāṃsavāḥ ||
english: Kaṣkiṣā, Kaṣpiṣā, Yevāṣā — this one here; sandy, dusty particles rushing, eager as desired cows.

sanskrit: adṛṣṭān na dṛṣṭān | dṛṣṭām̐ adṛṣṭān dhanapate jahīndrasya vadhena ||
english: The unseen, and also the seen — the seen and the unseen: slay them, O lord of wealth, with the weapon of Indra.

sanskrit: etāś ca viśvarūpāś ca gṛdhrāḥ kokāś ca te hatāḥ ||
english: These and those of every form — the vultures and the cuckoos too are slain.

sanskrit: kāme kāmayasva mā pratīcī prati mā bhava | mām anu pra te mano vatsā pākeva dhāvatu ||
english: O Desire, desire me; turn toward me, come back to me; may your mind run after me like a calf toward its innocent dam.

sanskrit: abhīle abhimādany asau mām abhi mādyatu | vidma patatriṇyā vayam iṣuke nāmakaṃ tava ||
english: O Abhīlā, O Abhimādanī — may that one become intoxicated with me; we know, O flying one, the name-charm of your arrow.

sanskrit: ahaṃ te mana ā dade mano manomuṣir yathā | mayi te mana āhitaṃ ratha iva rathavāhane ||
english: I take your mind to myself, like a mind-stealer stealing the mind; your mind is set in me like a chariot in the chariot-bearer.

sanskrit: ud asau sūryo agān mahyam avatunā saha | ahaṃ viśāṃ purohito madhuhasto madhujihvo mayi vāg astu dharṇasī ||
english: That sun has risen together with my fortune; I am the priest of the clans — honey-handed, honey-tongued; may firm speech abide in me.

sanskrit: ahaṃ viśyena ketunā samakṣye mānuṣeṣv ā | asmākam astu kevalaṃ bṛhad diśo adhi viśveṣu rājasu ||
english: I become visible among humans with the banner of the clan-chief; may the great one be ours alone over all the directions, over all the kings.

sanskrit: svādoś cin mā svādīyāṃsaṃ madhoś cin madhumattaram | priyāś cit sakhyur antaram ādityāsaḥ kṛṇota mā ||
english: Sweeter than the sweet, more honey-like than honey, dearer than a dear friend's intimacy — O Ādityas, make me so.

sanskrit: agne brahma tvaṃ brahmāsi viddhi tvaṃ prāsmabhyaṃ brūhi | yadīdaṃ tathā bhaviṣyasi yadi vā nāthaitasya haviṣo vīha svāhā ||
english: O Agni, you are Brahman; know this — speak forth to us. If this shall be so, or if not, then be pleased with this oblation here. Svāhā!

sanskrit: vi pṛcche dyāvāpṛthivī vīndraṃ vi bṛhaspatim | vi devān yajñiyān pṛcche vy asaṃ jīvanāya kam ||
english: I question Heaven-and-Earth, I question Indra, I question Bṛhaspati; I question the gods worthy of sacrifice — for whom shall I live?

sanskrit: vijñānāyodyatā prastutā srug iyaṃ yama rājan havir idaṃ juṣasva | agatāsor haviṣo mādayasva nirṛtiṃ gacchatu yad gatāsoḥ ||
english: O King Yama, this ladle is raised up for knowledge, this oblation is set forth — be pleased with it. Be gladdened with the oblation for one whose life has not yet departed; let what belongs to the departed go to Nirṛti.

sanskrit: yat tvā māṃse apavavau yan manthe yad odane | agniṣ ṭvā viśvabheṣajas tasmāt pātv aṃhasaḥ ||
english: Whatever has sucked you out from the flesh, from the stirred drink, from the cooked food — may Agni, the universal healer, protect you from that sin.

sanskrit: yas tvā vāta āvāty adharād uttarād uta | āpo yā viśvaśaṃbhuvas tās tvā pātv aṃhasaḥ ||
english: The wind that blows upon you from below and from above — may the waters that bring universal well-being protect you from sin.

sanskrit: apa tvan mṛtyuṃ nirṛtim apa yakṣmaṃ ni dadhmasi | yathā tvam arapā asa udojā uttaro bhuvaḥ ||
english: Death from you, Nirṛti from you, wasting disease — we press them down away from you, so that you may be free of wounds, full of upward strength, and superior.

sanskrit: vaiśvānaro raśmibhir naḥ punātu vātaḥ prāṇeneṣiro nabhobhiḥ | dyāvāpṛthivī payasā payasvatī ṛtāvarī yajñiye mā punītām ||
english: May Vaiśvānara purify us with his rays; may the Wind, the vigorous one, purify us with breath and clouds; may Heaven-and-Earth, rich in milk, keepers of cosmic order, worthy of sacrifice, purify me.

sanskrit: prajāpatir ṛtubhiḥ pañcabhiḥ saṃvatsaro dhāmabhiḥ pātu viśvaiḥ | ihaiva prāṇaḥ sakhye no astu tam ātmani punar ā veśayāmi ||
english: May Prajāpati guard us with the five seasons, may the Year guard us with all its stations; may breath remain here with us in fellowship — I place it back again into the self.

sanskrit: vaiśvadevīṃ sūnṛtām ā rabhadhvaṃ śuddhā bhavantaḥ śucayaḥ pāvakāḥ | tayā gṛṇantaḥ sadhamādeṣu vayaṃ syāma patayo rayīṇām ||
english: Take hold of the truth-speech belonging to all the gods, being pure, clean, and purifying; praising with it in the communal rejoicings, may we become masters of riches.

sanskrit: vaiśvānarīṃ varcasa ā rabhadhvaṃ yasyā āśās tanvo vītapṛṣṭhāḥ | īḍayeha sadhamādaṃ madanto jyok paśyema sūryam uccarantam ||
english: Take hold of the splendor belonging to all men, whose spreading forms have backs filled with light. Praising here, rejoicing in the communal festivity, may we long behold the sun rising.

sanskrit: avatkaṃ mama bheṣajam avatkaṃ parivācanam | narācy asi mā tudo vanvānā rogabheṣajam ||
english: The Avatka plant is my remedy, the Avatka plant is my surrounding incantation; you are of human nature — do not pierce me, being the healer of disease.

sanskrit: śambhuleham ihā hara tam u kṣīrā ud asyati | tad āsrāvasya bheṣajaṃ tad u rogam anīnaśat ||
english: Bring the Śambhuleha plant hither — the milk shoots it upward; that is the remedy for the flowing wound, and it has indeed destroyed the disease.

sanskrit: nadīṣu naḍvalāsu kumbheṣu kalaśeṣu ca pratīṣecanabheṣajam | tat te kṛṇomi bheṣajam addhi māṃsaṃ pibodakaṃ paṭpaṭiṅgaṃ vipaścalaṃ vi paśya ||
english: In the rivers, in the reed beds, in pots and in jars — the remedy by sprinkling: that remedy I make for you. Eat flesh, drink water, O Paṭpaṭiṅga, O Vipaścala — look clearly!

sanskrit: avidāma yad aicchāma piśācakṣayaṇaṃ haviḥ | tena kravyādo hanmaḥ sarvāś ca yātudhānyāḥ ||
english: We have found what we sought — the oblation that destroys the Piśācas; with it we smite the flesh-eaters and all the she-sorcerers.

sanskrit: icchanti tvā padātaya icchanti rathinas tvā | krīṇanti gobhir aśvair amṛtasyeva vā asi ||
english: The foot-soldiers desire you, the chariot-warriors desire you; they buy you with cows and horses — it is as if you were immortality itself.

sanskrit: amamri nāma bheṣajaṃ pṛthivyā adhy udbhṛtam | vaktā tan mahyam abravīd idaṃ ha pārayād iti ||
english: The remedy named Amamri, lifted up from the earth — a speaker told that to me: "This alone will carry you across."

sanskrit: cakṣur asi puruṣasya cakṣur goś cakṣur arvataḥ | cakṣur bhūtasya bhavyasya cakṣur apsarasām asi ||
english: You are the eye of man, the eye of the cow, the eye of the horse; you are the eye of what has been and what shall be, the eye of the Apsarases.

sanskrit: cakṣur asi suparṇasya cakṣur aher atho śunaḥ | cakṣuḥ sarvasya paśyato 'tho yad viśvam ejati ||
english: You are the eye of the eagle, the eye of the serpent, and also of the dog; you are the eye of all that sees, and of all that stirs in the universe.

sanskrit: ādadānaṃ sahasrākṣaṃ pratispāśanam abruvam | darśaya mā yātudhānān darśaya yātudhānyāḥ ||
english: I addressed the thousand-eyed one who seizes and ensnares: "Show me the sorcerers — show me the she-sorcerers."
